## Description

Add observation codes for height, respiratory rate, pain score, standing blood pressure, fundal height and fetal heart rate, and the key labs LDL cholesterol, eGFR, urine albumin/creatinine ratio, haemoglobin, ferritin, potassium, sodium, TSH, vitamin D and platelets. BMI is calculated from the latest weight and height, never stored as typed. Each code has a fixed unit and a reference range; a reading outside it is flagged in words (High, Low, with the range) on the chart. Nurse intake can enter height and respiratory rate. Patient 360 returns the latest reading and the trend for every code that has readings.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1.** Every new code has one unit and a reference range, and a value outside the range is returned with a High or Low flag and the range text.
- [ ] **AC2.** BMI is shown only when a weight and a height exist, uses the latest of each and states the date of the older one.
- [ ] **AC3.** Nurse intake saves height and respiratory rate with the same refusal of impossible values as the other vitals.
- [ ] **AC4.** Patient 360 returns a trend for each code with two or more readings, oldest first, with the source of each point.
- [ ] **AC5.** shortcut: reference ranges are one adult set (children's vitals keep the age bands of #956) and wait for clinical sign-off.

## Definition of Done

All acceptance criteria above, **plus** the cross-cutting X1–X8 checklist in [docs/05-delivery](../../README.md#definition-of-done-every-ticket).
